data.description: Rulings 2026-08-14 (sequence/org-settings-design.md iteration 3; design contract prototypes/pipeline-v1.1 v1.15 #org/organizers). (1) Role legend as ruled — Owner / Organizer / Ops / Reviewer, one capability line each — rendered on the Organizers surface and live under the invite modal's role picker (the Reviewer line says sign-in only, assign work in Evaluation). UI 'Organizer' maps to schema program_lead; write the mapping down once where roles render. (2) Permission model: the org-settings surface is visible to Owner + org-wide Organizers only; only the Owner removes members; Organizer and up invite. Enforce server-side, reflect in UI (permission-aware action column exactly as the prototype demonstrates). (3) Owner transfer, safe and simple: Owner-only action on their own row; eligible recipients are org-wide Organizers who have signed in; confirm requires the organization name typed back; the flip is immediate and atomic, old owner becomes Organizer, both notified by mail (outbox rules), recorded to audit_log. (4) Stale seats: a seat scoped to an ended conference never expires silently — banner on the Organizers surface + data for the Org Home attention line. Builds directly on MRQ-207's removal-cascade and scoped-invite work — coordinate, do not duplicate.
data.title: Organizer governance: role legend, Owner-only removal, owner transfer, stale seats

data.body:
MRQ-211 (PR #267) landed the named activity-recording seam you can call for the org admin lens.

src/lib/org-activity.ts:
  recordOrgActivity(db, entry)      — write one row now
  orgActivityStatement(db, entry)   — compose into your existing batch(); use this when the change itself is batched, so the record and the change share a transaction
  orgActor(auth)                    — actorKind/actorPersonId from the credential

entry = { orgId (required), eventId (optional — set it when the action is scoped to one conference; the lens resolves the name by join), actorKind, actorPersonId, action, entityType, entityId, before?, after?, now, requestId }.

Action names are constants in src/lib/activity-copy.ts — ORG_ACTIVITY_ACTIONS. Two are already defined and already read correctly in the lens; the writers are yours: org.defaults_changed (payload { changed: string[] }) and org.ownership_transferred (before { name }, after { name }).

Two things worth knowing:
- The org lens queries org_id, NOT a list of action names, so anything you write through the seam appears without touching the reader. An action the copy module has never met degrades to a readable sentence rather than a blank row (there is a test).
- If the subject of your action is a person (ownership transfer, a seat change), record entityType 'person' with their person_id — that is what puts it on their CRM feed (lens two) as well, with no extra work.

Also: migration 0019 makes audit_log.event_id nullable and adds org_id (a row must be scoped to at least one). If you touch audit_log, rebase onto that.
